lead: six people at that table have known each other for twenty years. you brought each of them in, one at a time, from outside. nobody sitting there has ever put that together.
sun: what you built there is a structure rather than a warmth. a night that does not move, a house that is open, an order in which news travels, an arrangement for whoever is out of work this year — all of it went up early, at full height, and it has not been adjusted since. nobody has been let go, because nothing here was made with a way of letting anyone go.
moon: the searching face works outward. the pleasure is in the going and the finding out, and a person already inside the wall offers nothing further to find — so twenty years of appetite has gone on the next one, in corridors, on trains, at other people's parties. you arrive with somebody. you rarely arrive alone.
pull: every friendship in that room was fetched. the twenty years of knowing each other happened between them, on the evenings you were out finding the seventh.
tension: half the group would say you are fond of them and slightly outside it — never quite there, and they have the attendance to prove it. what they are counting is the evenings you spent away, and each of those evenings is where one of them came from. the group's account of its own beginning has no person in it. it just grew, they say, and they were there.
cost: a person you liked for one evening in a corridor has six friends for life by the autumn, and was never put to any kind of test. the six ended up with each other. the closeness in that room runs between people you introduced. twenty years of arrivals, and no year of being the one somebody went out to find.

lead: the place was finishing at the end of the year, and a hall of a hundred heard you get to your feet and say exactly what you would put in so that it would not.
sun: nothing you put up has a trial version in it. what you named standing in that hall was in place inside a month at full height — the money, the hours, the guarantee signed in your name — and eleven years on it carries the load it was sized for, with no bad season anybody inside has had to notice. the place is a condition of that town now, not a project of yours.
moon: what left you that night left whole, at the one volume you have, with a hundred people present to fix it. nothing of that size can be revised down afterwards. so the evening put two permanent things into your life, and the two do not amount to the same fact: an act with no undo in it, and a structure that has never once looked like failing.
pull: the minute is permanent because a hundred people heard it. the building is permanent because what you raise holds. only one of the two has been mentioned since.
tension: the evening is the story, and it gets told well — at every function, by people who were not in the hall, in your hearing. eleven years of standing orders and roofs and rotas are not a story, because none of it has produced an occasion. and qualifying any of it now would mean amending a promise a hundred witnesses watched you make whole, so what arrives instead is more of it, addressed to the man who stood up.
cost: a thing that was closing is open, and it opened because you made yourself the answer in one minute, in public, with nobody having to be talked round afterwards. most of that hall has moved away or died. what is left of the evening is a standing order, a key on your ring, and a building full of people who assume it was always going to be there.

lead: the saturday club took you on again inside a fortnight — a parent with a car, on the rota by the second week. you started it at twenty-six and nobody there has an occasion to learn that.
sun: the arrangement has not been altered in nine years. the age groups, the way the pitch gets booked, the way the subs get collected — none of it needed you present, and none carries a name. a structure is not attributed from the inside. nobody in a room works out who set it, because nothing about a room raises the question, and nine years away raised it no better than the years you were there.
moon: the nine years registered in you as an interval, so resuming cost nothing: no case to make, no re-founding, no account of the gap asked for at any door. you expected the thing to still be there and it was. what makes that easy is the same fact that makes it flat — no position was being kept, so nothing had to be handed over.
pull: you were readmitted to your own arrangement by three people with the authority to grant it, none of whom knew there was anything to grant.
tension: you read as a newish member with fixed views about how the club is run. keen, they say, and under it, certain of things for somebody who turned up last year. nothing pushes against it: the pitch is booked, the subs come in, and a thing that works produces no evening on which anyone asks where it came from. each season somebody asks, kindly, whether you would like to help with the summer thing you invented.
cost: you can leave something standing for nine years, arrive from another country, and be inside it again by the second saturday, with no permission asked and none needed. your twenties are in the arrangement instead of in anybody. what you resumed is membership, and the ease of getting it is the same fact as the anonymity.

lead: eight years dead, and everyone who misses her still has somewhere to go and stand inside what she was. the roof, the shortfall and the boiler are yours, and nobody has set those two facts beside each other.
sun: you kept the house. keeping is a monthly payment, a bill each winter, a week of your summer up a ladder. nothing has been arranged into a shrine — two people live in it, a grandson's post comes there, a niece's boxes are in the small room, and the whole family goes at the year's end. the place holds, so it is a condition of their lives, and a condition is not an event.
moon: at the distance most of them stand at, it is simply the family home, a soft thing carrying on by itself. closer in there is a specific number of people taking specific amounts, and the number grows every year — a new partner, a cousin's friend for a summer, somebody between flats. nobody applied and nobody has been refused, because no edge was drawn for anyone to be outside of.
pull: what everyone has left of her is a room, kept by a payment out of your account every month. thirty people are standing in it and not one has seen the figure.
tension: proposing terms would land as a move against her. rent, a sale, a limit on who stays — it arrives in that family as an attempt to shut the last place she is still ordinary in, and money is heard as the wrong subject in a room understood as memory. so the arrangement only widens. they say you always loved that house, and they say it warmly, standing inside eight years of your work.
cost: everybody who lost her has a place where she is not in the past tense, which most families lose inside a year. you have not once been in that house as one of the mourners. you are the one who arrives early to put the heating on and leaves after the last car, and no year of the eight has been yours to spend on her.
